subCadenceSyntheticTap.finding: A synthetic press/release shorter than one 30 Hz interval was coalesced to the newest boost-off value, so the server did not observe boost-on. This is a selection limitation, not a finalized product rule.

singleBrowserMemorySample.warning: This is one CDP sample, not a peak, slope, browser-process RSS, export/import memory measurement, or leak result.

supported: The built browser connected to and rendered the disposable current P0 server.
Browser-player action production remained independent and periodic at both configured candidates.
A realistic drag sent steering plus boost-on and a later boost-off at both candidates.
The current reference maintained approximately 1x scheduler progress with zero reported dropped simulated-time debt near the final sample.
notSupported: A final choice between 30 Hz and 60 Hz.
Trusted-LAN, laptop, desktop, owner-trainer, Debian VM, or Ryzen 7 2700 performance.
A causal comparison between the two short display windows, which occurred at different world states.
Meeting the final display target: both sampled frame windows were below 25 fps and had p95 intervals above 40 ms.
Raw event-stream preservation, browser-memory peaks, or screenshot evidence.

timingBoundary: Browser CDP monotonic timestamps define every interval. Codex permission prompts, tool waits, model analysis time, host startup and deliberate host downtime are outside each bounded event window.
